Subject: SIG/CAIQ follow-up: subprocessor residency and KMS provenance

Hi Lukas,

Thanks for the demo last week. Horton Health's procurement and security teams are moving our SIG/CAIQ review forward and have a couple of clarifying asks around third-party residency and crypto provenance before we can complete our procurement packet. Can you provide the following artifacts?

1) A current subprocessor roster that lists country of operation and the purpose (storage/monitoring/analytics/keys) for each supplier.
2) A short diagram and narrative of how customer encryption keys are managed when customers use Redwood-managed keys versus customer-managed KMS (BYOK). We need to understand where keys are held, whether plaintext is ever transmitted to subprocessors, and any KMS/HSM vendors used.
3) Copies of FIPS / HSM attestations or vendor security statements that show the module/provider we rely on for Redwood-managed keys.
4) A short, procurement-ready paragraph that states the residency guarantees (if any) and whether we support customer-controlled key residency in specific cloud regions.

Target timeline: can you get this to us by COB Tuesday (2026-11-10)? If you need a different cadence (e.g., we can accept a partial pack and a follow-up), let me know.

Appreciate it — this is the last item on our checklist.

Best,
Daniel
Daniel Park

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T11:30:00Z
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ follow-up: subprocessor residency and KMS provenance

Adding details and attaching initial artifacts.

Lukas / Soojin — I pulled the current roster and a draft KMS diagram. Attached: redwood_subprocessor_roster_20261108.csv and kms_keyflow_diagram_v2.pdf (stubs). Notes:

- Subprocessor roster includes cloud providers (AWS/GCP), monitoring (Datadog), identity (Okta), analytics (Amplitude), and logging/backup partners. Column 4 marks whether the subprocessor handles encrypted material or keys.
- For Redwood-managed keys we use AWS KMS backed by CloudHSM (where available). We rely on vendor attestations for the underlying HSMs (we've linked the vendor FIPS 140-2 statements in the related_links below).
- Important: Redwood never transmits customer plaintext to a third-party subprocessor as part of normal inference. Customer plaintext is processed in-memory on the serving runtime and we do not persist unencrypted input to external vendor storage.
- BYOK (customer-managed KMS): customers can configure external KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) using an endpoint integration or by deploying a private connector. In BYOK mode keys remain in the customer's KMS/HSM and Redwood never exports or stores the key material.

Draft procurement paragraph (please review, this is what we should send to Horton):
"Redwood Inference supports both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys (BYOK). For Redwood-managed keys, cryptographic keys are stored in the cloud provider's key management service and backed by HSM(s) that meet FIPS 140-2 validation; Redwood does not share plaintext with subprocessors. For customers requiring strict residency, Dedicated and Private deployment options allow keys to remain in region-specific customer-owned infrastructure or customer-managed KMS/HSMs. Specific residency commitments are governed by the chosen deployment contract and region selection."

If that reads OK I will: 1) attach vendor attestation links and 2) produce a signed vendor attestation summary PDF by end of day tomorrow.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Information Security — Redwood Inference

Lukas / Marissa — thank you, this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Two small asks before we close our packet:

1) Can you include a one-paragraph, procurement-ready statement explicitly confirming that in BYOK mode the customer key material is never exported from their KMS/HSM and that Redwood only performs cryptographic operations over the network with the customer's KMS? We need that language for our legal team.
2) For the Redwood-managed keys sentence, can you add the specific HSM vendor name you rely on for CloudHSM-backed keys so we can cross-reference vendor attestations?

If you can send those two items (a signed one-paragraph statement and the vendor name) by tomorrow morning our SIG reviewer will mark this as closed. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Best,
Daniel
CloudOps Lead, Horton Health
